memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of
their God. Because they present the food offerings to the LORD, the
food of their God, they are to be holy'" - Lev 21:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the reason behind every rule in this chapter. The priests
handled the offerings that belonged to God. Their hands touched what
was sacred. So their lives could not casually contradict what their
hands were doing.

To "profane" God's name means to treat as common something that is
holy. It happens when a person who represents God lives in a way that
makes others think less of Him. The world watches. It always has.

This is a sobering thought for every believer, not just for pastors
and leaders. If you carry the name of Christ, your life is saying
something about Him whether you intend it or not. Jesus said, let your
light shine before others so that they may see your good deeds and
glorify your Father in heaven (Matt 5:16).

But please hear this too. Our holiness is not the foundation of our
acceptance; it is the fruit of it. We do not live carefully so that
God will love us. We live carefully because He already does, and
because His name is precious to us.

Dear reader, someone in your home, office or neighbourhood forms an
opinion about Jesus partly by watching you. Live gently under that
weight of grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does my daily conduct make God's name attractive or common to those
   around me?
2. Where is there a gap between what I say I believe and how I live?
3. Am I pursuing holiness out of gratitude rather than fear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, Your name is precious. Forgive me for the times I have made it
look small by my choices, and shape me into someone who honours You
well. Amen.
